quizzes.title: Computer Basics
quizzes.subject: Computer Fundamentals
quizzes.description: Hardware, software, memory, networks and security essentials every computing student should know.

questions.text: Which component is considered the "brain" of the computer?
questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit executes instructions and coordinates the other components.

questions.text: What does RAM stand for?
questions.explanation: RAM is Random Access Memory: fast, temporary working storage.

questions.text: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A printer produces output from the computer. The others send input to it.

questions.text: What is the decimal number 5 in binary?
questions.explanation: 5 = 4 + 1, which is 101 in binary.

questions.text: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an operating system kernel and family of OSes. Chrome and Word are applications; Python is a language.

questions.text: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is HyperText Markup Language, the standard language for structuring web pages.

questions.text: Which storage unit is the largest?
questions.explanation: KB < MB < GB < TB. Each step is roughly 1,000 (or 1,024) times larger.

questions.text: What is the main job of an operating system?
questions.explanation: The OS manages memory, processes, files and devices so applications can run.

questions.text: Which of the following is volatile memory?
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is removed, so it is volatile.

questions.text: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a resource on the web.

questions.text: Which shortcut copies selected text on most Windows computers?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + Z undoes.

questions.text: Which protocol is used to load web pages securely?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS, which encrypts traffic between browser and server.

questions.text: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a programming language. Ethernet and Bluetooth are networking standards; JPEG is an image format.

questions.text: Which storage device has no moving parts?
questions.explanation: An SSD stores data in flash memory chips, so nothing spins or moves.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a firewall?
questions.explanation: A firewall filters network traffic according to security rules.

questions.text: Which of the following is application software?
questions.explanation: Excel is an application used by people to do tasks. Windows, BIOS and drivers are system software.

questions.text: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explanation: One byte is 8 bits.

questions.text: Which of these is a web browser?
questions.explanation: Firefox is a web browser.

questions.text: What does "WWW" stand for in a web address?
questions.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web.

questions.text: Which type of malware attaches itself to files and spreads when they are shared?
questions.explanation: A computer virus attaches to legitimate files and replicates when those files are run or shared.

quizzes.title: Programming Fundamentals
quizzes.subject: Programming
quizzes.description: Variables, loops, functions, arrays and problem solving basics.

questions.text: What does a variable do in a program?
options: Stores a value that can change
questions.explanation: A variable is a named storage location whose value can change while the program runs.

questions.text: Which loop is best when you know in advance how many times to repeat?
questions.explanation: A for loop has an initialiser, condition and update, so it suits a known number of repeats.

questions.text: What is the index of the first element of an array in most languages (C, Java, JavaScript, Python)?
questions.explanation: Array indexes start at 0, so the last index is length - 1.

questions.text: What is a function?
options: A reusable block of code that performs a task
questions.explanation: Functions let you write code once and call it many times, optionally with parameters and a return value.

questions.text: Which data type is best for storing true or false?
questions.explanation: A Boolean holds exactly one of two values: true or false.

questions.text: What is the result of 7 % 3?
questions.explanation: The % (modulus) operator returns the remainder: 7 divided by 3 leaves 1.

questions.text: What is an algorithm?
options: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of steps that solves a problem.

questions.text: Which statement runs different code depending on a condition?
questions.explanation: if / else is a conditional (selection) statement.

questions.text: What is a syntax error?
options: A wrong answer produced at run time
A mistake in the rules of the language, found before the program runs
questions.explanation: Syntax errors break the grammar of the language, so the code cannot be compiled or parsed.

questions.text: What does a compiler do?
options: Translates source code into machine code
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine code (or bytecode) before it runs.

questions.text: What is an infinite loop?
options: A loop that runs exactly once
A loop that never meets its stopping condition
questions.explanation: If the loop condition never becomes false, the loop keeps repeating forever.

questions.text: What is 'debugging'?
options: Finding and fixing errors in code
questions.explanation: Debugging is the process of locating and fixing bugs.

questions.text: In 'function add(a, b) { return a + b; }', what are a and b called?
questions.explanation: a and b are parameters: placeholders for the values passed in when the function is called.

questions.text: Which of these is a valid way to describe 'pseudocode'?
options: Code that only runs on phones
questions.explanation: Pseudocode mixes plain language and programming structure to plan logic without strict syntax.

questions.text: What does 'return' do inside a function?
options: Sends a value back and ends the function
questions.explanation: return ends the function and hands a value back to the caller.

quizzes.title: Web Development Basics
quizzes.subject: Web Development
quizzes.description: HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap 5 and JavaScript essentials for building responsive pages.

questions.text: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is the standard markup language that gives web pages their structure.

questions.text: Which tag creates the largest heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the top-level heading; <h6> is the smallest.

questions.text: Which CSS property changes the text colour?
questions.explanation: The color property sets the colour of text.

questions.text: Which HTML attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.explanation: alt text helps screen-reader users and is shown if the image fails to load.

questions.text: In Bootstrap 5, which class creates a responsive fixed-width container?
questions.explanation: The .container class centres content and changes its max-width at each breakpoint.

questions.text: How many columns does Bootstrap's grid system use per row?
questions.explanation: Bootstrap divides every row into 12 equal columns.

questions.text: Which JavaScript method finds an element by its id?
questions.explanation: document.getElementById('x') returns the element whose id is x.

questions.text: Which symbol is used for an id selector in CSS?
questions.explanation: #name selects the element with id="name"; .name selects by class.

questions.text: Where is the safest place to put a <script> that reads page elements?
options: At the end of <body> (or with defer)
questions.explanation: Scripts at the end of the body, or loaded with defer, run after the elements exist.

questions.text: What does the viewport meta tag do?
options: Makes the page scale correctly on mobile screens
Adds a keyword list for search engines
questions.explanation: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> is essential for responsive design.

questions.text: Which CSS feature lets a layout change at different screen widths?
questions.explanation: @media rules apply styles only when conditions such as screen width are met.

questions.text: Which method saves data in the browser that stays after the tab is closed?
questions.explanation: localStorage persists until cleared; sessionStorage is erased when the tab closes.

questions.text: What does 'addEventListener' do?
options: Runs a function when an event such as a click happens
questions.explanation: It registers a handler that runs whenever the named event occurs on the element.

questions.text: Which HTML element is used for the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> is the semantic element for a block of navigation links.

questions.text: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS = Cascading Style Sheets, used to style HTML.

quizzes.title: Databases and SQL
quizzes.subject: Databases
quizzes.description: Tables, keys, SQL statements and relational database concepts.

questions.text: What does SQL stand for?
questions.explanation: SQL is the standard language for working with relational databases.

questions.text: Which SQL statement reads data from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT retrieves rows (and columns) from one or more tables.

questions.text: What is a primary key?
options: The first column of every table
A column that uniquely identifies each row
questions.explanation: A primary key's values are unique and not null, so each row can be identified.

questions.text: Which clause filters rows in a SELECT statement?
questions.explanation: WHERE keeps only the rows that satisfy a condition.

questions.text: Which statement adds a new row to a table?
questions.explanation: INSERT INTO table (cols) VALUES (...) adds a row.

questions.text: What is a foreign key?
options: A column that refers to the primary key of another table
A key used by another country's database
questions.explanation: A foreign key links rows in one table to rows in another.

questions.text: Which clause sorts the results?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY col ASC|DESC sorts the output.

questions.text: Which aggregate function counts rows?
questions.explanation: COUNT() returns the number of rows (or non-null values).

questions.text: What does DBMS stand for?
questions.explanation: A DBMS (e.g. MySQL, PostgreSQL) stores, manages and secures data.

questions.text: Which statement removes a table and its data completely?
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE deletes the table definition and all its data.

questions.text: Which command changes existing values in a table?
questions.explanation: UPDATE table SET col = value WHERE ... changes existing rows.

questions.text: What is a 'table' in a relational database?
options: A collection of rows and columns
questions.explanation: A table stores related data in rows (records) and columns (fields).

questions.text: What does 'normalisation' aim to do?
options: Reduce duplicated data and improve consistency
questions.explanation: Normalisation organises tables so each fact is stored once.

questions.text: Which keyword removes duplicate values from the SELECT result?
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT col returns each different value once.

questions.text: Which JOIN returns only rows that have matching values in both tables?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps rows where the join condition matches in both tables.

quizzes.title: Computer Networks
quizzes.subject: Networking
quizzes.description: IP addressing, protocols, devices and the internet.

questions.text: What does 'IP' in IP address stand for?
questions.explanation: An IP address identifies a device on a network using the Internet Protocol.

questions.text: Which device connects different networks and forwards packets between them?
questions.explanation: A router forwards data between networks, for example your home network and the internet.

questions.text: Which protocol is used to load secure web pages?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS encryption.

questions.text: What does DNS do?
options: Translates domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System maps names like example.com to IP addresses.

questions.text: What does LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: A LAN connects devices in a small area such as a lab, home or office.

questions.text: Which protocol is mainly used to send e-mail?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends mail between servers.

questions.text: What is bandwidth?
options: The maximum amount of data that can be transferred in a given time
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the capacity of a connection, usually measured in Mbps or Gbps.

questions.text: Which topology connects every device to one central switch or hub?
questions.explanation: In a star topology, all devices connect to a central device.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a firewall?
options: Monitor and filter network traffic according to rules
questions.explanation: A firewall allows or blocks traffic based on security rules.

questions.text: Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 has four numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots.

questions.text: What does DHCP do?
options: Automatically assigns IP addresses to devices
questions.explanation: DHCP gives devices an IP address (and other settings) when they join a network.

questions.text: What does 'WWW' refer to?
options: The system of linked web pages accessed via the internet
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web is a service that runs on top of the internet.

questions.text: Which command checks whether another computer is reachable?
questions.explanation: ping sends small test packets and reports the response time.

questions.text: What is a MAC address?
options: A hardware address burned into a network interface
questions.explanation: A MAC address is a unique identifier assigned to a network card.

questions.text: Which layer-based model has seven layers?
questions.explanation: The OSI reference model describes networking in seven layers.
